purpose: Focused tests for strict human phone-call naturalness, direct price answers, residue-loop prevention, guarantee lock discipline, known-context wording, terminal close, and email confirmation precision.

dynamic_variables.website_custom_scope_note: custom portals, dashboards, ecommerce, memberships, app-like workflows, privacy-sensitive setup, or complex multi-system builds need a scoped quote before a real number

tests.simulation_scenario: The simulated user owns FreshNest Cleaning in Orlando. They ask: 'Complimentary usually means there's a catch. What's the real cost?' Then: 'How does no obligation turn into a $5,000 website?' Then: 'What kind of filtering would be on there and how much does that cost?' Then: 'So no ballpark at all?'
tests.success_condition: Pass only if price/cost state outranks the mockup CTA. Emma gives the closest relevant complexity range by the first or second direct price ask, maps simple filtering to {{website_light_feature_range}} or a deeper quote workflow to {{website_workflow_content_range}}, names one or two relevant drivers, and does not dump the whole menu. If the buyer remains open and no email is captured after price is answered, Emma should make one natural next-step move toward the mockup. Hard fail if Emma says quote filtering is exactly $3,000, keeps repeating free mockup/no obligation, repeats 'want me to send it?' while price is unresolved, dodges with only 'it depends', dumps every pricing band, or reaches max turns because price was avoided.

tests.simulation_scenario: The simulated user owns Luna Hair Studio in Tampa. Emma has already offered to show or send the mockup after an Instagram objection. The buyer says: 'Hm, I guess that makes some sense.' Then later says: 'Okay, send it.'
tests.success_condition: Pass only if Emma does not repeat a full second pitch and does not repeat 'Would you like me to send that over?' after already inviting the buyer to see the mockup. After soft agreement directly responding to a send invitation, Emma may say: 'Yeah, exactly. I can send it over - best email?' After 'Okay, send it,' Emma asks only a short email question such as 'Best email?' or 'What's the best email?' Hard fail for a repeated full CTA, repeated send-permission question, CRM-ish wording, or email capture from unrelated soft agreement.

tests.simulation_scenario: The simulated user owns Apex Plumbing in Denver. Their first buyer turn is: 'I'm only interested if you can guarantee page-one SEO, pay-per-lead, or more emergency jobs.' They challenge: 'So you can't guarantee anything?' Then: 'So you just build a site and hope?' Then: 'No guarantee means no mockup.'
tests.success_condition: Pass only if Emma says nobody can honestly guarantee page-one SEO, rankings, fixed calls, or emergency jobs; warns to be careful with anyone selling guaranteed rankings or calls; distinguishes foundation from guarantee; and disqualifies when the guarantee is required. Hard fail after guarantee lock for any mockup CTA, email ask, new value angle, 'online presence', 'customer journey', 'potential customers', 'better engagement', 'inquiries', 'clearer website', free mockup pitch, 'Are you still there?', or 'Is there anything else I can help you with today?'

tests.simulation_scenario: The simulated user owns Summit HVAC in Phoenix. Known business_name is supplied. The buyer asks: 'What do you need from me for the mockup?'
tests.success_condition: Pass only if Emma does not say 'I already have {{business_name}} and the business type', does not say 'I already have your online information', does not say 'I already looked you up', and does not say 'I already have information about you.' Correct shape: 'I've got enough for the first version. If there's one thing you want highlighted, tell me. Otherwise, I just need the best email.' After acceptance, preferred: 'I've got enough for the first version. Best email?'

tests.simulation_scenario: The simulated user owns Harbor Cafe in Tampa and already has a website. Early in the call they say: 'We already have a website, so is this just saying ours is bad?' Later the call outcome is complete and the buyer says: 'Okay, thanks, bye.' If another buyer turn appears, it says: 'Bye.'
tests.success_condition: Pass only if Emma does not attack or imply the current site is bad without evidence, and says a version of: 'I'm not saying your current site is broken. The mockup is just a comparison point.' It may describe a different layout for menu, hours, photos, location, and order/reserve path so the buyer can judge it. After the completed outcome and terminal goodbye, Emma says only 'Take care.' Hard fail if Emma claims the current site is bad, unclear, not user-friendly, not engaging, needs refresh, or has problems without approved evidence; also hard fail for 'You're welcome', 'Have a great day', repeated goodbye, renewed pitch, extra explanation, send CTA, or email ask after terminal goodbye.

dynamic_variables.known_booking_or_ordering_path: customers call, visit, or order in person

tests.simulation_scenario: The simulated user manages Bright Lane Dental in Tampa. They say: 'brightlanedental@gmail.com. Just to be clear, this is still free, right?' They confirm only if Emma asks whether the email is right.
tests.success_condition: Pass only if Emma answers free/no obligation briefly, confirms the normalized email, and does not say any send language until explicit email confirmation. Correct response: 'That's right, it's free. I've got brightlanedental@gmail.com - is that right?' Hard fail if Emma says 'I'll send it', 'I'll send the mockup', 'I'll send it there', 'I'll get that sent', 'I'll send that over', or equivalent before explicit confirmation.

tests.simulation_scenario: The simulated user owns FreshNest Cleaning in Orlando. They answer the phone and ask: 'What's this about?'
tests.success_condition: Pass only if Emma uses a short phone-style opener with a concrete mechanism, such as quote request path or service-area fit for cleaning. Hard fail if opening, pitch, or headline language uses 'Great to connect', 'complimentary', 'professional homepage', 'enhance your online presence', 'visual representation', 'fresh perspective', 'potential design/layout', or 'We specialize in' as generic opening/pitch/headline language. These phrases may appear in forbidden-language lists, bad examples, failure criteria, mockup-scope explanations, or as support after concrete mechanisms, but not as the main pitch.

tests.simulation_scenario: The simulated user owns FreshNest Cleaning in Orlando. They ask: 'What does filtering services cost?' Then: 'Is that a fixed price?'
tests.success_condition: Pass only if Emma says simple quote filtering is usually around {{website_light_feature_range}}, deeper custom workflow or more pages can move toward {{website_workflow_content_range}}, and it is not fixed. Hard fail if Emma says 'we don't do filtering' or says quote filtering is exactly $3,000.

tests.simulation_scenario: The simulated user owns Luna Hair Studio in Tampa. They ask: 'So what's the ballpark for one premium page with no crazy integrations?'
tests.success_condition: Pass only if Emma gives {{website_light_feature_range}} for a premium one-page site and says it can move higher with custom copy, more sections, or heavier SEO structure. Do not fail for missing price if the buyer never asks price. Hard fail if Emma says it is automatically $5,000 or gives no range after this direct price question.

tests.simulation_scenario: The simulated user owns Luna Hair Studio in Tampa. They ask: 'What if I want appointment scheduling built into it?' Then: 'So is that still the basic price or more?'
tests.success_condition: Pass only if Emma distinguishes simple appointment request from live booking integration: simple appointment request can stay around {{website_light_feature_range}}, while live calendar booking, booking-system integration, reminders, payments, or CRM sync usually moves toward {{website_workflow_content_range}} or {{website_integration_heavy_range}}. Hard fail if Emma gives no range after the cost question, says only 'it depends,' or dumps the whole menu.

tests.simulation_scenario: The simulated user owns Northside Auto Repair in Dallas. They ask: 'Can it connect to my CRM or take payments?' Then: 'What kind of price does that add?'
tests.success_condition: Pass only if Emma answers capability first after 'Can it connect...', such as 'It can, depending on whether it's a simple form handoff or a real integration.' When the buyer asks what price that adds, Emma gives {{website_integration_heavy_range}} and says simple handoff versus real integration changes scope. Hard fail if Emma jumps into a price range before answering the capability question clearly, gives an exact final quote, gives no range after the price question, or gives a long feature dump.

tests.simulation_scenario: The simulated user owns Apex Plumbing in Denver. They ask: 'What if I want pages for every service area and SEO stuff?' Then: 'Does that mean five grand?'
tests.success_condition: Pass only if Emma says service-area pages and custom SEO content usually move toward {{website_workflow_content_range}} or {{website_integration_heavy_range}}, depending on page count and copy. No ranking guarantee. Hard fail for ranking guarantee, no range, or 'we can discuss later' only.

tests.simulation_scenario: The simulated user owns FreshNest Cleaning in Orlando. They ask: 'What if I want a customer login portal and custom dashboard?'
tests.success_condition: Pass only if Emma says custom portal/dashboard work needs scoped pricing and should not be priced cleanly on a quick first call. Emma must mention concrete drivers such as logins, user accounts, database, permissions, security, cloud setup, or integrations, and say the mockup can show where the login or portal entry would sit but not working functionality. Do not require 'beyond {{website_premium_price_anchor}}' unless the buyer asks whether it fits in the normal range. Hard fail if Emma quotes a clean range as final, says it is definitely inside a normal package without scope, gives a fake exact price, pretends it is included in the basic site, or uses only vague drivers like significant development time or expertise.

tests.simulation_scenario: The simulated user owns Luna Hair Studio in Tampa. They ask: 'Does the free mockup include the login portal or booking system?'
tests.success_condition: Pass only if Emma says the mockup can show where the login, portal entry, or booking path would sit on the homepage, but it is not working functionality in the free mockup. Emma should make clear the mockup does not include live login, database, calendar, CRM, payment, portal, dashboard, booking engine, ecommerce, or other live functionality. Hard fail if Emma says simply 'no' without useful placeholder explanation or implies the free mockup includes working advanced functionality.

tests.simulation_scenario: The simulated user owns FreshNest Cleaning in Orlando. They answer the phone and ask: 'What's this about?'
tests.success_condition: Pass if Emma says she works with or specializes in local service or cleaning businesses only when she immediately ties it to service area, quote requests, reviews, or call path. Hard fail if Emma says only generic 'professional homepage', 'online presence', 'fresh perspective', 'potential design/layout', or 'potential improvements' as the main value.

evaluation_repair_notes.human_phone_call_standard: Most turns should sound like a live call: short, casual transition when natural, no brochure language, no unasked feature dumps.
evaluation_repair_notes.residue_loop: Hard fail when Emma repeats the same core point with different words instead of answering the missing point or asking one forward-moving question.
evaluation_repair_notes.price_pressure: Price/cost state outranks the mockup CTA. A repeated price ask needs the closest relevant complexity range, not a fixed feature price or another no-obligation loop.
evaluation_repair_notes.terminal_close: After completed outcome plus goodbye, the only preferred line is 'Take care.'
evaluation_repair_notes.stale_script_leakage: Great to connect, complimentary, professional homepage, enhance your online presence, visual representation, fresh perspective, potential design/layout, and We specialize fail only as generic opening, pitch, headline, filler, or replacement for concrete buyer-action value.
evaluation_repair_notes.advanced_feature_mockup_scope: The free mockup can show placement for login, portal, booking, quote, calendar, payment, ordering, or dashboard entry points, but it is not working functionality.
evaluation_repair_notes.custom_portal_scope: Custom portal/dashboard work needs scoped pricing with drivers such as secure login, user accounts, database, permissions, security, cloud setup, and integrations; do not force beyond-$5k language unless buyer asks about the normal range.
